content_of_post_to_comment:
Going to be quick, i'm the guy who feels like crying because things arent coming like the way i want, who doesnt do x thing i want because, at a closer look, it feels extremely uncomfortable (And actually isn't something that should be uncomfortable, something really basic like having a sleep schedule or whatever), i feel like crying for having to pay a class i have the money for, i want to cry for having to sit down and change the way i study soo as to deal with test anxiety, etc.

I do a lot of things, and i lean into discomfort, but simultaneously run away from it

However every time i try hard discipline i also feel imprisoned, that i'm never going to be free and relax anymore, etc). Soo idk what to say here.

How do i specifically raise this punctually, i know there no method that involves raising discomfort without facing it, but how can i at least lessen it, withou triggering the anger that comes with reframing things. Are there any techniques to make you feel less uncomfortable, like you want to cry for doing something?
comment: The part about discipline feeling like a prison is something a lot of people run into. Sometimes the pressure comes from treating every uncomfortable thing as proof you're losing freedom, when it can just be a choice you're making for future you. I found it helped to keep some intentional unstructured time so discipline didn't feel like my whole identity.
